body:
VERIFIED against the code, 2026-08-18. Found during the annotations reconnaissance; no
existing finding covers it.

`cps/annotations.py::ingest_bookmarks` (def at line 349) builds its row at line 424:

    row = ub.Annotation(
        user_id=..., annotation_id=..., book_id=...,
        highlighted_text=..., highlight_color=..., note_text=...,
        content_id=..., start_container_path=..., ... , source="kobo",
    )

Fifteen fields, and `annotation_type` is not among them. The LIVE capture path does set it
— `cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:315`, `ann.annotation_type = native_type`.
So the two paths that write the same table disagree: a row that arrives over the live
PATCH carries a type, and the identical annotation recovered from the device's own sqlite
carries NULL.

Why this is worse than an untidy column, and why it is ORDERING-CRITICAL:

F-b1004e is the finding that the importer drops every dogear and note-only bookmark
(`WHERE Text IS NOT NULL AND Text != ''`). The obvious fix is to admit them. But the
importer is the ONLY recovery path that exists — the device uploads a delta and never
re-offers (F-a66189, and both `kobo_annotation_seed_capture*` tables are measured at 0
rows, so nothing has ever backfilled). So the moment F-b1004e lands, dogears begin
arriving through this constructor — and they will arrive TYPE-NULL, indistinguishable
from highlights, in the one code path whose entire purpose is to recover data faithfully.

Fixing F-b1004e without this first therefore converts "dogears are missing" into "dogears
are present but mistyped", which is harder to detect and harder to undo than the absence.

Fix direction: set `annotation_type` in `ingest_bookmarks` from the same derivation the
live path uses, so the two writers agree; then land F-b1004e. Consider a test that asserts
the two write paths produce the same column set for the same logical annotation — the
class here is "two writers to one table drifted", not this single column.

--- ⚠️ THE FIGURES BELOW DO NOT REPRODUCE — SEE F-724452 (2026-08-19) ---

Re-measured 2026-08-19 against local-dev/config/app.db, the database cwn-local
actually serves: it has 632 rows across 19 books (621 webreader, 8 koreader,
3 kobo) and NO annotation_type column at all, so no distribution over that
column can be measured there. The counts in this section were probably taken
from cwn-mine's throwaway config under /tmp, which is gone. Treat them as
unsourced. The CODE claims in this finding were re-verified and stand: the
importer never sets annotation_type, and the live path sets it only when the
payload carries a `type` key.

--- ORIGINAL, UNSOURCED FIGURES, KEPT SO THE CORRECTION HAS SOMETHING TO POINT AT ---

The scale is far larger than the importer alone, and the filing above under-stated it.

  annotation_type distribution across all 628 server annotations:
      (null)      615
      dogear       10
      highlight     3

98% of the live annotation store is typed NULL. Two causes, and only one is the importer:

1. `annotation_type` is ONE DAY OLD — introduced 2026-08-17 by #1685 ("Stage 0 of two-way
   annotation sync"). Every row captured before that predates the column.
2. The live path sets it CONDITIONALLY — `cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:312`
   is `if "type" in payload:`, so a PATCH whose body omits `type` also leaves it NULL.
3. The importer never sets it at all (the original finding).

Book 404 shows the before/after split cleanly: 4 rows typed `dogear` and 4 typed NULL,
same book, same `source='kobo'` — the difference is which side of #1685 they were captured on.

Consequences this measurement adds:

- **Any feature keyed on `annotation_type` currently operates on ~2% coverage.** That is a
  trap for anything downstream that filters or renders by type: it will silently behave as
  though the user has almost no dogears, because 615 rows cannot say what they are.
- **The ordering argument against F-b1004e still holds and is now sharper.** Newly imported
  dogears would join 615 existing NULLs rather than standing out, so the mistyping would be
  invisible rather than merely wrong.
- **A backfill is needed, not just a forward fix.** Fixing the importer and the conditional
  only types rows captured from now on. The 615 historical rows stay NULL unless something
  derives their type — which is possible for many of them, since a Kobo dogear has no
  highlighted text while a highlight does (`highlighted_text` is populated for all four of
  book 350's rows, so text presence alone will not separate every case — this needs its own
  derivation rule, not an assumption).

resolution.note: Fixed in #1774: ingest_bookmarks now sets annotation_type=to_storage_type(bm.annotation_type) (cps/annotations.py:427), so the importer and the live PATCH path agree. The ordering hazard this finding named is also discharged -- F-b1004e landed in the same PR, so dogears arrive typed rather than TYPE-NULL. Held by tests/unit/test_annotation_type_vocabulary.py::test_no_annotation_constructor_leaves_the_type_unset. Mutation re-verified independently 2026-08-22: blanking the annotation_type keyword in annotation_portable.py fails exactly that test (1 failed, 20 passed).

title: The KoboReader.sqlite importer never sets annotation_type, so every recovered row is typed NULL
